_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: Recruiting trials admit an ultra-rare fusion-driven sarcoma (extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma) under molecular eligibility criteria while the registry conditions field a diagnosis search reads never names the histology, so the patient is inside the trial's own definition and outside its index; and the obvious remedy, a keyword reachability map, is worse than no map, because both trials adjudicated as REFUSING this disease would have passed a keyword screen.

blockers.summary: §7 Data availability says the two 2026-08-09 artifacts "name the API base only". `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` names NO API base and no URL of any kind, so a reader cannot reproduce §4.1 — the paper's only non-US finding — at all.
blockers.evidence: At the pin, `research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` has `"_retrieval": {"route": "workflow_dispatch of .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml with an inline targets_json manifest; the runner executes scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py and publishes to the literature-cache branch", "actions_run_id": 31333672478, "slug": "non-us-trial-registries-2026-08-09", "date_et": "2026-08-09"}` — four keys, no `api` field. `grep -o 'http[s]*://[^" ]*'` over the whole file returns ZERO matches: the file contains no URL at all. Its `endpoints` rows carry only registry names ("ISRCTN (UK)", "WHO ICTRP", "EU CTIS", "ANZCTR (Australia/New Zealand)", "jRCT (Japan)") and `queries: ["chondrosarcoma", "sarcoma AND fusion"]`. By contrast the sibling the same sentence covers, `emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json`, DOES carry `"api": "ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies)"` — so the claim is true of one of "the other two" and false of the other. The only ISRCTN endpoint URL committed anywhere in the tree is `"isrctn_emc": "https://www.isrctn.com/api/query/format/who?q=extraskeletal+myxoid+chondrosarcoma"` in `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json` — a DIFFERENT query (the histology, not `chondrosarcoma`) from a DIFFERENT sweep (2026-08-07), so it does not rescue the sentence. The consequence is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: §4.1's exclusion finding, §5's "the query that ran there was the parent term chondrosarcoma", and the 403/TLS endpoint reasoning all depend on knowing which endpoint answered and with what query, and the deposit records neither.
blockers.fix: Rewrite the last sentence of §7 to say what each artifact actually records, e.g.: "Only the first records a retrieval URL per record. The adjudication file ran from an inline manifest that was never committed and names the API base (`https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies`); the non-US sweep ran from an inline manifest that was never committed and records the run id, the registry names and the two queries, but no endpoint URL." Better still, add the five endpoint URLs to `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` from Actions run 31333672478's manifest and keep the sentence as written.

blockers.summary: §7's list of URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep is incomplete and two of the three paths it names do not exist. The omitted fourth manifest is the one behind the UNFIELDED sarcoma screen that §2 and §3 rely on.
blockers.evidence: `research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json` -> `retrieval.runs` lists FOUR runs, each with its `targets_file`: `emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json` (run 31175763521), `research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json` (run 31176517524, slug `ct-reverify-frontier-2026-08-07`), `emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json` (run 31176811772) and `emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json` (run 31179088283). §7 names three and omits the frontier manifest. That omission is not incidental: the frontier run produced the payload `ct_sarcoma_2026_new`, which the sweep's own `instruments` block describes as "sarcoma + fusion/transcription factor/degrader, unfielded so eligibility text is included". I checked each manifest's keys at the pin — `ct_sarcoma_2026_new` is present ONLY in `lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json` and in none of the three files §7 names. The paper leans on that payload twice: §2's "one sarcoma screen was unfielded and did carry it", and §2/§3's "eligibility text was retrieved for three of those nine … the third inside the unfielded screen" (that third is NCT06988475, whose `retrieved_from.payload` is `ct_sarcoma_2026_new`). SECOND defect in the same sentence: the shorthand "`research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json`, `-c3.json` and `-c4.json`" resolves literally to `emc-clinical-sweep-targets-c3.json` and `-c4.json`, and `git ls-tree` at the pin shows no such paths — the real files are `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json` and `-c4.json` (the stem drops "targets"), and `git log --diff-filter=A` shows they were created under that name on 2026-08-07 and never renamed.
blockers.fix: Replace the sentence with the four full paths: "The URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep are `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json`, `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json`, `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json` and — for the unfielded sarcoma screen — `research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json`." Never abbreviate a deposit path to a suffix.

blockers.summary: §3's "Those are counts of the four records adjudicated here" attaches an admit-count of two-plus-one to a set of four that neither §2, §5 nor the adjudication deposit agrees with. The deposit's four adjudicated records contain ONE trial that admits and offers treatment, not two.
blockers.evidence: §3 reads "Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits and offers enrolment in an observational cohort. Those are counts of the four records adjudicated here, not of the registry." The committed deposit `research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json` -> `summary` says `{"candidates_adjudicated": 4, "admits_and_is_interventional": 1, "admits_but_is_observational": 1, "refused": 2}`, and its four `adjudications` are NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101 and NCT07188532 — NCT05918640 (the second treatment-admitting trial) is NOT among them; it comes from `fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json` -> `task_2_widened_search.confirmed_fusion_family_defined`. `systems/graph/artifacts.json` restates the deposit the same way for ART-TRIAL-REACH-ADJUDICATION: "Two admit this disease and only one of those is interventional." The paper's own §5 uses the correct version — "Four candidates were adjudicated: two admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse" — so one short paper attaches "four … adjudicated" to two incompatible sets with two different treatment-admit counts (2 in §3, 1 in §5). The alternative reading, that "the four records" means the four rows of §3's table, is refuted by the paper's own §2: "The basket records in §3's third row are the exception and are not adjudicated". Under every reading the sentence is wrong: either the count is wrong for the four adjudicated candidates, or the word "adjudicated" is wrong for the four table rows. `git log -S` shows the sentence was added on 2026-09-02 in 8c574fc as a denominator disclaimer.
blockers.fix: Stop using "adjudicated" for the table rows and name the set: "Those are counts of the four records in this table, not of the registry." §5's sentence is correct and should be left alone; it and §3 then describe different sets in different words, which is the point.

p1s.summary: No gate anywhere in this repository reads an ISRCTN identifier. Both ISRCTN numbers in §4.1 are correct at this commit, but a mistyped digit would pass every gate — the identical hole `lint_citations.py` records having closed for arXiv in AUT-PD-057.
p1s.evidence: `research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py` -> `PATTERNS` has exactly six kinds: PMID, PMCID, DOI, NCT, GEO, ARXIV. There is no ISRCTN pattern. `git grep -ln "ISRCTN" <pin> -- '*.py' '*.yml' '*.yaml' '*.sh'` returns NOTHING — no linter, no test, no workflow, no script in the tree contains the string. The gate does scan this document (PROSE_SUFFIXES = ('.md',) over `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`), and its six NCT/PMID identifiers do anchor: all six NCTs and PMID 32967265 appear in tracked `.json` fetch products. The two ISRCTNs are simply invisible to it. The linter's own AUT-PD-057 comment describes this exact state for arXiv before 2026-08-28: "EVERY arXiv IDENTIFIER IN THIS REPOSITORY WAS OUTSIDE THE GATE ENTIRELY — not baselined, not anchored, not counted; simply invisible." Both ids check out today: `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` records `"id": "ISRCTN07742377"` with the verbatim exclusion criterion and `"id": "ISRCTN60791336"` with "Its exclusion list names 'Chondrosarcoma' as an ineligible subtype".
p1s.fix: Add `"ISRCTN": (r"\bISRCTN(\d{8})\b", r"isrctn\.com/(ISRCTN\d{8})")` to `PATTERNS` in `research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py`. All three ISRCTNs in the tree (ISRCTN07742377, ISRCTN60791336, ISRCTN52235823 — 8 digits each) already appear in `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json`, so the gate lands green with no ledger baseline; a mutation test flipping one digit must go red.

p1s.summary: Not one number in this paper is bound to any artifact. `lint_consistency.py` scans the document only for superseded-value patterns; `pinned-figures.json` has 99 `artifact_figures` entries and none names this paper or any of its three deposit artifacts.
p1s.evidence: `research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json` lists `research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md` in `targets` (29 entries), which `lint_consistency.check_superseded` uses — that only re-checks the 81 registered `superseded` patterns against it. `check_artifact_figures` is driven by `artifact_figures`, and over its 99 entries the substring counts in the registry are: `trial-reachability` = 1 (the `targets` row only), `fet-fusion-trial-eligibility` = 0, `non-us-registry-sweep` = 0, `emc-clinical-sweep` = 0. So nothing pins 42 conditions, five NR4A3-term studies, 1,159 unique studies, 400/199/526, seven-vs-ten conditions, twelve/five/three/seven damaged records, n=73, n=5500 or age 1-30. The repository's own committed census agrees and quantifies it: `research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json` records for this document `{"sentences": 87, "covered": 0, "with_a_number": 20, "with_a_number_covered": 0, "uncovered": 87, "uncovered_with_a_number": 20}` — zero of 87 sentences and zero of 20 numeric sentences are read by any instrument. `claim_coverage.py`'s docstring is explicit that this is the remaining blocker risk: "The uncovered set IS the remaining blocker risk".
p1s.fix: Add `artifact_figures` entries with `must_appear_in: ["research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md"]` for at least the four numbers a future edit could silently falsify: NCT06239272's condition count (`fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json` -> `task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3.trials[1].listed_conditions`, len 42), NCT06571734's seven retrieved conditions (adjudication file -> `adjudications[0].listed_conditions`, len 7) against the sweep's ten, the NR4A3 term-search count (`task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies`, len 5) and `retrieval.unique_studies_indexed` (1159).

p2s.summary: §2 discloses the transport caveat for NCT05918640's quoted criterion but not for NCT06239272's, whose eligibility text carries NINE removal markers, was equally never re-fetched after the fix, and supplies the age bound the abstract and §4.1 use to bound the whole finding.
p2s.evidence: §2: "NCT05918640's eligibility text carries one such marker and was not re-fetched after the fix, so the criterion quoted for it in §3 is the sentence the artifact records as transport-clean rather than a re-read one." In `fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json`, NCT05918640 has `removal_markers_in_eligibility_text: 1` and NCT06239272 has `removal_markers_in_eligibility_text: 9`; both carry `verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean: true`, and neither is among the four candidates re-fetched on 2026-08-09 (`emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json` -> `adjudications` = NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101, NCT07188532). The NCT06239272 sentence, "Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS", is what the abstract ("bounds age at 1 to 30 years at the diagnostic biopsy, so the gap reported here is not universal") and §4.1 rest on. Nothing quoted is damaged — the caveat is simply disclosed for one record and silently omitted for the other, and the omitted one carries nine times the marker count.

p2s.summary: §3 renders one of NCT06571734's seven retrieved conditions in a different word order from the field it presents as retrieved.
p2s.evidence: §3: "all seven as retrieved 2026-08-09: metastatic leiomyosarcoma · unresectable leiomyosarcoma · bone sarcoma · translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma · synovial sarcomas · metastatic osteosarcoma · Ewing sarcoma". The deposit's `adjudications[0].listed_conditions` is `["Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma", "Unresectable Leiomyosarcoma", "Bone Sarcoma", "Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma", "Synovial Sarcomas", "Osteosarcoma Metastatic", "Ewing Sarcoma"]` — the sixth entry is "Osteosarcoma Metastatic", not "metastatic osteosarcoma". The other six are in source order and wording. The seven-versus-ten claim itself is exactly right: the 2026-08-07 fielded screen recorded ten (`task_2_widened_search.candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification[0].listed_conditions`, adding "Ewing Sarcoma Metastatic", "Sarcoma Metastatic", "Sarcoma of Bone").

p2s.summary: The front-matter `scope` accounts for three unread non-US endpoints; there are four. The fourth is disclosed in the abstract and §5 but not in `scope`.
p2s.evidence: `scope`: "Two further non-US registries refused automated access and a third failed at the TLS handshake; all three are reported as unread endpoints rather than as absences." `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` -> `endpoints` records five non-US endpoints, of which four went unread: EU CTIS (HTTP 403), ANZCTR (HTTP 403), jRCT (SSL handshake failure) and WHO ICTRP (HTTP 404, "THE URL WAS A GUESS AND IT WAS WRONG"). The abstract ("a fourth went unread because our own query URL was wrong") and §5 both disclose ICTRP; `scope` does not, so a reader who reads only the front matter counts three.

p2s.summary: §7 does not say where the evidence for the paper's one literature citation lives, though it is committed and excellent.
p2s.evidence: The abstract's "most often to EWSR1, next to TAF15, and rarely to FUS, TCF12 or TFG, as a review reports (PMID 32967265)" is fully anchored — `fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json` -> `task_2_widened_search._supporting_literature_read_in_the_same_ci_run` holds the retrieved full-text `verbatim`: "In the vast majority of cases (over 70%), NR4A3 fuses to … (EWSR1) … less frequently (about 20% of cases) to … (TAF15) … Rarer (<5%) NR4A3 fusion partners include FUS (alias TLS), TCF12 … and Transforming Growth Factor (TFG)", with `url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7563993/fullTextXML`, `retrieved_in: ct-reverify-c3b-2026-08-07 (Actions run 31176811772)`, `provenance: SECONDARY - this is a review`, and the note "EWSR1, TAF15 and FUS are the three FET-family genes; TCF12 and TFG are not" — which is also what makes §3's "admits … not when it is TCF12 or TFG" exact. `citation-article-types.json` independently records `article_types: ["Journal Article", "Review"]` for that PMID, so "as a review reports" is right. §7's inventory sentence covers only "every trial identifier, every verbatim criterion quoted, and every adjudication", so a reader is not told the fusion-partner quote is in the same file.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: "Five studies for the driver-gene term search could be a page-size artefact" — §3 already bounds it: the search returns whole records, is capped by response size rather than page size, and "five is what it returned, not what the registry holds". The deposit's `search_url` carries `pageSize=100`, so 5 is not a page limit.

"Two admitting trials is a count, not a floor" — the abstract, §2 and §5 all bound it by the saturated screen: `instruments` records `ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed` returning 400 studies and its manifest URL carries `pageSize=400`, so the screen came back at its page limit and is truncated, exactly as §5 says.

"A 403 might be read as a registry containing nothing" — §5 refuses that explicitly, and the deposit's `⚠_a_refusal_is_not_an_absence` says the same in stronger words; the ClinicalTrials.gov positive control in the same run is what makes the refusals readable, and the paper says so.
"The RECRUITING flags may be stale" — §5 names the worst case by NCT id, and it matches: `NCT03767075` carries `status_verified_date: "2024-04"`, `last_update_post_date: "2024-04-25"`.

"NCT06239272's age bound might be measured at enrolment, which would change who the exception covers" — the paper says at the diagnostic biopsy in both the abstract and §4.1, and the verbatim criterion is "Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS"; the structured fields (`minimum_age: null`, `maximum_age: "30 Years"`) would not have told a reader that.

"NCT07188532's listed molecular condition in Remedy 1 may be a recollection" — it is not: `task_2_widened_search.candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification[1].listed_conditions` is `["Ewing Sarcoma", "Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion"]`.

"Twelve lost records / five recoverable / three from the condition searches" — all three counts reproduce exactly: the union of `transport_integrity.unparseable_records` (10 unique ids) and `silently_damaged_records` (3) is 12; exactly five of the twelve reappear elsewhere in the same file with data (NCT05275426, NCT05836571, NCT06094101, NCT07188532, NCT07695311); the three from `ct_emc_all` + `ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma` are NCT00720174, NCT05355753 and NCT01189253, whose statuses in `research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json` are COMPLETED, TERMINATED and TERMINATED — "one completed and two terminated", all closed.

"The nine molecularly-defined records may be padded" — they are not: one master protocol (NCT05722886), seven DETERMINE arms (NCT05768178/05770037/05770102/05770544/05786716/06988475/07440290, of which NCT07440290 is NOT_YET_RECRUITING) and one separate basket trial (NCT03767075); `emc_in_listed_conditions` is false for all nine; and eligibility text was retrieved for exactly three, two by per-study URL and NCT06988475 inside the unfielded screen — precisely as §2 states.

"The fetcher defect may still be open" — `scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py` at the pin gates the stripper behind `_looks_structured()`, which sniffs the first non-space byte as well as the Content-Type so JSON/XML reach disk byte-for-byte; §2's "That defect has since been fixed at the fetcher" is accurate.

"Something here might be synthetic and unflagged" — nothing is. Every claim traces to a CI registry read; the paper cites no registry-curation artifact, and `research/data/emc-clinical-registry.json` contains zero `SAMPLE_SYNTHETIC` rows at this commit.
notes: Every identifier in the paper traces, and the sentences they are attached to say what the deposits say: nine identifiers (six NCT, two ISRCTN, one PMID), each with a committed fetch record, and the load-bearing fields — NCT06239272's 42 conditions with the histology at position 26, NCT06571734's seven-versus-ten condition lists, NCT05918640's four conditions and its verbatim FET criterion, NCT03767075's April-2024 verification, NCT07188532's molecular listed condition, and the PMC7563993 partner ranking — all reproduce field-for-field. The three blockers are all in the provenance apparatus rather than in the science: two are in §7, the section whose only job is to tell a reader where the evidence is, and one is a denominator sentence in §3 that collides with §5 and with the adjudication deposit. The coverage picture is the more uncomfortable finding. `lint_citations.py` reads this document and clears its NCTs and its PMID, but has no ISRCTN pattern and no gate in the tree does; `lint_claims.py` reads it through `systems/graph/publications.json`; `lint_consistency.py` reads it only for superseded patterns because `pinned-figures.json` binds none of its numbers to an artifact. The repository's own committed census puts a number on that — 87 sentences, 20 with a number, 0 covered — so a green build on this paper is a statement about six NCT strings and one PMID, and about nothing else it says.
